assertionCorrection.diagnosis: The new restore preflight intentionally reads the complete DNS-client inventory. The old disappearance assertion counted that as a stale per-interface read. Keep the stronger inventory preflight and assert exactly one complete query plus zero per-interface queries/mutations after the adapter disappears.

behavior: A successful complete DNS-client inventory distinguishes absent families from inspection failures and rejects duplicate/invalid client identities.
Up adapters with no DNS-client family are not configuration targets; physical flags and hardcoded runner names are not used for eligibility.

New snapshot bound4/bound6 fields record captured family coverage; legacy records retain their both-family contract. Half-present/nonboolean/empty coverage and inconsistent unused-family data are refused.
Newly exposed families are captured before effects without replacing earlier originals or first global DoH metadata.
Only captured families receive configuration/restoration writes; GUID/index identity is checked during capture and refreshed before each family write.
Recovery preflights every owned family before effects and retains originals if a required family disappears.
The independent oracle reads registry state separately; non-exposed families use explicit mode and private canonical dormant-state fingerprints, not DHCP guesses.
Source regressions cover no-DNS, IPv4-only/IPv6-only, failed complete inventory, new-family extension, persistence/capture faults, malformed flags, legacy records and identity races.

Each actual native run verified configured IPv4/IPv6 server lists and DoH policy on originally selected interfaces, ordinary DNS answers, exact original modes/static order/global DoH and dormant non-exposed state, snapshot removal and joined controller streams.
limitations: Real native qualification covers fresh hosted Windows AMD64/ARM64 DoH round trips; it does not qualify every Windows version, installed/signed packages or managed deployment.
Encrypted packet transport is not independently observed; DNSCrypt, failure/reboot and every original DNS-gate requirement remain open.
IPv4-only/IPv6-only, family activation, malformed snapshots and capture races are source-mock contracts; no real hotplug or protocol-binding change was performed.
